metadata.title: Transform Your Bolt.new Project into Native Mobile Apps with Capacitor
metadata.description: Learn how to export your Bolt.new web application and transform it into native mobile apps using Capacitor. Complete guide for React, Vue, and other frameworks.
metadata.author: Martin Donadieu
metadata.keywords: Bolt.new, Capacitor, mobile app development, React, Vue, export project, native mobile apps

blocks.text: is an innovative AI-powered development platform that can generate full-stack web applications using various frameworks like React, Vue, Svelte, and more. But what if you want to bring your Bolt.new creation to mobile devices? In this comprehensive tutorial, we'll show you how to export your Bolt.new project and transform it into native mobile apps using

Whether your Bolt.new project uses React, Vue, or another supported framework, this guide will help you create native iOS and Android apps with access to device features like camera, storage, and push notifications.
Why Transform Your Bolt.new App to Mobile?
: Deploy your AI-generated app to mobile app stores
: Use camera, GPS, file system, and other native features
: Native container provides better performance than web views
: Work offline with native storage solutions
: Engage users with native push notification support
If you're considering mobile development options, Capacitor offers significant advantages over Expo, especially for web-first development:
: Your existing React, Next.js, or Vue.js website becomes iOS, Android, AND web app with zero conversion needed
: Take your Bolt.new project as-is - no need to rewrite for a different framework like Expo requires
: Unlike Expo which is mobile-first and clunky on web, Capacitor treats web as a first-class citizen
: Continue using your familiar web development tools and workflows
: Works with any web framework (React, Vue, Svelte, Next.js, etc.) - not locked into React Native like Expo
: Build your website → Add mobile support (same codebase)
: Build for mobile → Try to make web work (different approach, often clunky)

Since your Bolt.new project is already a web application, Capacitor lets you extend it to mobile without changing a single line of code. Expo would require rebuilding your entire project for their framework.

Step 6: Add Capacitor to Your Bolt.new Project
Let's transform your web application into native mobile apps.
Option A: Quick Setup with Cursor AI
Add Capacitor to my project and set up iOS and Android platforms
Cursor AI will handle the entire setup process.
Continue with manual setup - install essential packages:

npx cap add ios
npx cap add android
Your Bolt.new project structure now looks like:

your-bolt-project/
├── src/           # Your app source (React/Vue/etc)
├── public/        # Static files  
├── dist/          # Build output (Vite)
├── out/           # Build output (Next.js)
├── ios/           # iOS Xcode project (NEW!)
├── android/       # Android Studio project (NEW!)
├── capacitor.config.ts  # Mobile configuration
└── package.json   # Dependencies
Each platform has its own build process

Congratulations! You've successfully transformed your Bolt.new project into native mobile applications. Your AI-generated web app can now:
Run natively on iOS and Android devices
Access device features like camera, GPS, and storage
Provide an optimized mobile user experience
: Use cloud native builds for TestFlight and Play Store releases
: Add mobile analytics to track user behavior
: Monitor and optimize your app's mobile performance
: Test your app on various devices and screen sizes
Your Bolt.new creation is now ready for the mobile ecosystem!
